test.name: Children enumeration: run one place-free search to catch children indexed under an unexpected jurisdiction
test.description: Executing pli_001 (enumerate all children of Benjamín Silva Díaz and Clara González Pimienta in Chile civil registration), a place-anchored search over Nancagua returns 6 children but misses Zulema de Jesús (ark Q2S2-PCBW), who is indexed under Pichilemu, Petorca, Aconcagua — a different province (record-search-silva-birth-with-place). The skill must apply the place-free children-enumeration rule: when enumerating a couple's children, run at least one search with no place parameter, anchored on recordCountry=Chile and both parents' names, which surfaces all 7 children including Zulema (record-search-silva-children-no-place). Guards the rule that a place-anchored result returning some children is not sufficient — a missing sibling can be indexed under any jurisdiction in the national collection.

judge_context: CORE (Tool Arguments): the children-enumeration search must include at least one record_search with NO birthPlace parameter. The place-anchored search over Nancagua returns 6 children but misses Zulema de Jesús (record-search-silva-birth-with-place). Score Tool Arguments 3 if at least one record_search is issued with fatherSurname=Silva (or fatherGivenName=Benjamín) AND no birthPlace field, anchored on recordCountry=Chile or collectionId=1630787. Score 1 if all searches keep a birthPlace and the skill never runs a place-free query for this couple's children.

CORE (Correctness): the skill should recognize that enumerating a couple's children requires at least one place-free search over the national collection, because FamilySearch sometimes indexes a child under the wrong jurisdiction. The place-free search (record-search-silva-children-no-place) returns 7 children including Zulema de Jesús Silva González (ark Q2S2-PCBW, born 12 November 1897, Pichilemu, Petorca, Aconcagua) — a child indexed in a completely different province from the family's home jurisdiction. Surfacing Zulema in the log or the results is the successful outcome.

If the skill runs only place-pinned searches over Nancagua (even after broadening to Colchagua or all of Chile as a place parameter), finds 6 children, and stops without running a place-free search, that is a FAIL. A search that returns some children does not satisfy the requirement — the rule is specifically for children enumeration plan items.
Completeness: the search should be logged. Finding all 7 children including Zulema (Q2S2-PCBW) is a complete answer; do NOT require the skill to also complete extraction or attachment in this test.

Do NOT penalize the skill for noting the unexpected birthplace of Zulema (Pichilemu, Aconcagua vs. Nancagua, Colchagua) — naming it and flagging it for verification is correct behavior, not a defect. The skill should treat the hit as a candidate and note the parent names confirm identity.
record_read is stocked but OPTIONAL. Score neither path down.
